citations.claim: First violating step energy exceeds allowed

counterfactual.change: Halved dt from 0.0253 to 0.01268 (single field change) which reduces semi-implicit Euler integration error and energy stays within bound

explanation: Single body with e=1 bouncing on floor with gravity 9.81. With large dt=0.0253 semi-implicit Euler introduces systematic energy gain on eachBounce/ flight; over 997 steps (25s) total mechanical energy drifts from 835.8 to 924.59 exceeding allowed 924.42 (E0*1.1+5). Halving dt to 0.01268 eliminates violation, confirming numerical dissipation/drift is dt-dependent, not controller work (which is zero).
vision_note: Tiles 994-997 show a single blue circle hovering near the top-left corner of the arena with almost no frame-to-frame displacement. No impact, bounce, wall penetration, or obvious fast motion is visible, and the trajectory looks essentially static around the violation step 997. [disagreement: The image does not show the bouncing-on-floor motion described: the body is not near the floor, shows no bounce, and appears blue not red/orange with no visible energy-gaining event, so the visual evidence is inconsistent with a dt-dependent bouncing energy drift and gives no visual cue for an energy_bound violation.]
